report.summary: Chunk 3 of 13: defines UNMEASURED tuple, platform_supported(), ContainmentUnavailable exception, and ctypes signatures for Windows API.
risks: WHY_READ_ATTRIBUTES | low | Claim about os.fstat(1) needing FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES and pytest redirecting to os.devnull is uncheckable; no code in chunk verifies this.
UNMEASURED entry 'handle-value reuse' | low | States spawning is assumed single-threaded; no multi-threading guard visible in chunk.
UNMEASURED entry 'log AFTER the run' | low | Claims window after child death is not measured; no code in chunk addresses this.
UNMEASURED entry 'GrantedAccess' | low | States child's copy access mask was measured by operation, not proven for every class; no verification in chunk.

handoff.purpose: Defines UNMEASURED risks, ContainmentUnavailable exception, platform_supported(), and ctypes signatures for Windows API.

symbols.name: WHY_READ_ATTRIBUTES
symbols.note: Tuple containing one string explaining why FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES is granted.

symbols.name: UNMEASURED
symbols.note: Tuple of strings listing containment aspects not measured. Documented to grow; test must ensure original entries never disappear.

symbols.name: ContainmentUnavailable
symbols.note: Exception raised when containment cannot be established. Docstring says 'NEVER downgraded silently'.

symbols.name: platform_supported
symbols.note: Returns True only on Windows (os.name == 'nt'). Docstring says 'True only where the measured mechanism exists. No optimism.'

claims.text: FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES is granted because os.fstat(1) needs it and pytest silently redirects all output to os.devnull when it fails -- measured: exit 0 with zero bytes captured. It is a read right on a Low-labelled file the contained child could have opened itself, so no capability crosses that it did not already have.
claims.why: The claim references os.fstat(1), pytest behavior, and measurements not present in this chunk. No code verifies these assertions.

claims.text: Surfaces this module does NOT claim to have measured. Stated so that silence is never mistaken for coverage. This tuple GROWS when a mechanism lands; a test fails if the three original entries ever disappear.
claims.why: Claims about tests failing when original entries disappear are not verifiable from this chunk; no test code is present.

claims.text: named pipes: a Medium server with a Low client was not measured, and MIC is not documented here as a reliable IPC boundary
claims.why: No code in chunk measures named pipes or MIC boundaries.

claims.text: network egress: a Low process still has a full network stack
claims.why: No code in chunk addresses network egress restrictions.

claims.text: reading: MIC is a write-up barrier and does not restrict reads at all
claims.why: No code in chunk discusses MIC read restrictions.

claims.text: log path disclosure: the child can recover the log's full path from the inherited handle via GetFinalPathNameByHandle (measured, it works). The path is disclosed; the file is not reachable by any other route while the handle is open, because the share mode refuses a second opener
claims.why: No code in chunk implements or verifies log path disclosure or share mode.

claims.text: the log AFTER the run: once this process closes the inherited handle the share-mode guard is gone. The child is dead by then (Job Object, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE) and the scratch tree is removed through the guarded walker, but a surviving Low writer racing that window was not measured
claims.why: No code in chunk implements Job Object, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, guarded walker, or measures the racing window.

claims.text: handle-value reuse: the allowlist is verified immediately before CreateProcessAsUserW, on handles this process owns and does not close. A second thread closing one of them inside that window, and the value being reissued for another object, is not defended against -- spawning is assumed single-threaded
claims.why: No code in chunk implements handle allowlist, CreateProcessAsUserW call, or multi-threading guards.

claims.text: GrantedAccess is the kernel's accounting of OUR handle. That the child's copy carries the same mask was measured by OPERATION (read and truncate were refused in the child), not proven for every operation class
claims.why: No code in chunk measures GrantedAccess or child's operation restrictions.

claims.text: Containment could not be established. NEVER downgraded silently. A caller that asked for containment and cannot have it must decide what that means. This module refuses to decide by handing back an uncontained process that looks contained -- which is the failure mode the whole file exists to remove.
claims.why: The class definition and docstring are present and consistent with the claim.

claims.text: True only where the measured mechanism exists. No optimism.
claims.why: The function returns os.name == 'nt', which is True only on Windows, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Without them ctypes assumes c_int and truncates the 64-bit pseudo-handle from GetCurrentProcess; that surfaces as ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE and reads exactly like 'the OS refused us', which cost a debugging round the first time this was measured.
claims.why: No code in chunk demonstrates the error or the debugging round.

observations.what: WHY_READ_ATTRIBUTES references os.fstat(1) and pytest behavior not present in this chunk.
UNMEASURED tuple documents unmeasured vectors but no code in chunk verifies any of the claims.
platform_supported() returns os.name == 'nt', but no other platform checks are present.
Windows ctypes signatures are declared but not used in this chunk.
